newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi says he does not want car incentives.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi says he does not want car incentives.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said he did not believe special financial incentives were the best way to revive flagging car sales in Itly, newspapers reported on Sunday.
Industrialists have called on the government to follow France's lead in devising an incentive scheme to encourage Italians to trade in their old cars for new ones.
"I have followed the French experience step by step and I have serious doubts about the final outcome," Prodi said while attending the inauguration of a motor show in Bologna on Saturday.
Prodi said an incentive scheme could boost sales temporarily but there could be a slump after the measures were phased out.
"The French government now has the worry of having to handle 60,000 potential job losses in a sector as concentrated as cars," he added.

He said the answer to the industry's problems was a revival in the overall economy. "I have a long term objective and even the revival of sales is not unconnected from the restructuring of the whole economy," said Prodi.
